supporting_observations.claim: A RouteWise-named updater ran from Kim Nguyen's user-local AppData directory, rather than the Program Files location listed for the approved RouteWise updater in the inventory.

The updater initiated repeated connections through the proxy to update.routewise.co:443. The observed destination is routewise.co, whereas the inventory lists update.routewise.com as the approved update host.
The proxy connections occurred repeatedly at roughly five-minute intervals, from 13:37:54 through 14:07:36 UTC, and the updater process subsequently exited.

The noncanonical executable location and the difference between the observed .co destination and the inventory's approved .com hostname are suspicious discrepancies, but do not alone establish that the activity was malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT tunnels and metadata, not the encrypted application payload or the content exchanged with the destination.
The provided records do not include the updater's hash, signature-validation result, installation provenance, or a reputation assessment for update.routewise.co.
The available records show the periodic requests and their process attribution, but do not establish what the updater downloaded or whether it executed any downloaded content.
claims_not_established: Whether update.routewise.co is controlled by the legitimate RouteWise provider or is malicious.
Whether the user-local updater binary is genuine, modified, or unauthorized.
Whether any data was exfiltrated or malicious payload was downloaded or executed.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire the updater binary and determine its hash, signature validity, file origin, and installation or execution history.
Verify update.routewise.co ownership and reputation, and compare its TLS certificate and server details with the legitimate RouteWise update service.
Review proxy or endpoint TLS-inspection and download records, if available, for the content exchanged during the observed sessions.
Check whether other endpoints ran the same binary or contacted the same hostname.
unrelated_findings: A Dropbox updater executable ran as SYSTEM on WS-KNGUYEN-01; Dropbox is not among the approved file-sharing or cloud-storage services listed in the inventory. This is separate from the alerted RouteWise connections. (T135-00176, T135-00177)

Kim Nguyen's account authenticated from 10.52.10.24 to WS-PBECKER-01, with corresponding Kerberos activity from that address. The supplied records do not establish why this occurred; investigate separately from the alerted outbound connections. (T135-00273, T135-00274, T135-00275)
